approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from accepted scored molecules. It chooses parents from high-scoring population quantiles and fills a surplus pool using connected-fragment crossover or successive local mutations, with bounded retries and saturation recovery. Direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is disabled. Stable canonical identities and duplicate rejection govern pool admission. A Gaussian posterior trained on the full accepted archive uses integer-count Morgan fingerprints and generalized Tanimoto similarity; correlated score draws select distinct candidates from the pool. Accepted feedback updates the archive and a bounded population of the best observed molecules.
approach.novelty: Add a narrow sulfur-environment introduction gate at final pool admission. It preserves the source experiment's neutral sulfur envelope and exact local signatures, including permitted terminal carbon-sulfur double bonds. For a one-parent proposal, outside-envelope signature counts may not exceed that parent's counts. For crossover, each signature may not exceed its largest count in either actual generating parent. Rejected products trigger the existing bounded refill loop. The new question is transfer from a single-source tabu walk to two-parent graph pools with posterior selection. Completed siblings altered crossover or posterior components; pending siblings alter donor construction or ordinary continuation. This Child retains those Parent mechanisms and tests only the sulfur admission rule.

observed_bottleneck: The current Parent n-62daf219c70a admits a small but exercised channel of new outside-envelope sulfur environments. Its three actual summary.json/run.log pairs are complete, with macro mean 0.5956696497334577 and population SD 0.02659287062806747. Its molecular report records N=S-containing output alongside a productive carbonyl-thione family, arguing against a sulfur-wide ban. A read-only application of the exact n-93cd9a000278 classifier/signature to all 69600 logged Parent pool entries, using maximum signature counts across actual scored generating parents, finds 94 positive-D opportunities: 76 mutation and 18 crossover, across twelve of fifteen sessions. They contain 111 positive signature-count units. Five such products are actually evaluated, all in seed two; one beats its best parent and improves the incumbent. Seven emissions contain any outside-envelope sulfur. Thirty-nine of 133 outside-envelope pool products have D=0 and would remain allowed as inherited chemistry. Permitted terminal carbon-double sulfur occurs in 2821 pool-center and 185 emitted-center observations. Thus the target is selective prevention of an observed introduction channel, with sparse exposure and real useful excluded paths; it is not evidence that all unusual sulfur lowers score. In the complete L16 n-93cd9a000278 versus n-9f7c7ec50039 comparison, the gate rejected 766/5307 valid novel neighbors, of which 760 would otherwise pass tabu, and retained sulfur in 2821 emissions while removing targeted introductions. Mean change was +0.005864965090889351, but seed deltas were +0.01556482448764307, -0.061423458899526995 and +0.06345352968455198; macro population SD rose from 0.004890242222897396 to 0.04677410123358011. Historical L01 halogen redirection n-079af8c4a86b and carbonyl protection n-9bee44b1c9c3 activated their constraints yet lost mean 0.005164911501081633 and 0.034753022975410296. Current crossover removal n-767d2ce08797 also lost endpoint quality despite more local wins. These are direct cautions against equating a narrower chemical channel or local yield with endpoint benefit.
hypothesis: Reject a final valid canonically novel offspring before pool admission exactly when an outside-envelope sulfur local signature has greater multiplicity than its maximum across the actual accepted scored generating parents, using the fixed neutral-sulfur envelope and exact signature from n-93cd9a000278, then continue the inherited bounded pool-generation loop.

finding_summary.headline: The sulfur gate contains new violations and retains the mean, but misses the performance-gain goal
finding_summary.insights: The narrow admission rule transfers from a single-source walk to scored-parent pools and can preserve the panel mean without establishing a useful endpoint gain. Its real exposure is sparse and uneven, and the Parent included one targeted introduction that improved its incumbent, so rejecting this chemistry is not synonymous with removing only unproductive paths. The exact per-signature maximum is validated separately from a parental sum; synthetic boundary cases are not search evidence. The relative rule would still allow inherited signatures within their reference counts: an inherited outside-envelope Parent offspring became the deco_hop incumbent at 0.617802. Zero absolute violations here therefore does not establish universal cleanliness. The emitted chemistry retains permitted thiocarbonyls, thioethers and oxides, but also 93 sulfur-halogen observations and unresolved non-sulfur reactivity, ring geometry and stereochemistry. Conventional thioether and sulfur-free improving alternatives constrain those concerns without proving a broader filter would help. The earlier source gate still has its favorable mean alongside a losing seed and greater dispersion; this new result neither pools nor rewrites that evidence.
finding_summary.results: The gate rejects exactly 130 of 69730 valid novel pool candidates with positive sulfur-signature excess. All 69,600 admitted members and 4,350 evaluated offspring have zero excess against their actual scored parents. Rejections affect 81 batches containing 810 real accepted evaluations; every pool and announced batch completes. 3 sessions have no positive exposure and reproduce their Parent trajectories. Absolute outside-envelope sulfur also falls from seven Parent emissions to zero Child emissions under these clean inherited states, while sulfur remains in 1100 Child observations versus 935 Parent observations. Mean endpoint score rises from 0.595670 to 0.596453, a change of only +0.000783. That meets the registered -0.002 noninferiority boundary but misses the separate +0.002 gain goal. Seed changes are +0.017686, +0.002307 and -0.017643; six task-seed endpoints improve, six decline and three tie. Macro population dispersion rises from 0.026593 to 0.033970.

molecular.headline: Sulfur stays inside the narrow envelope; aromatic leaders still carry reactive attachments and difficult ring geometry
molecular.overall_character: Node n-1744a1494180 emits compact aromatic amides and sulfur/carbonyl analogues, linked nitrogen-rich heterocycles, aryl-substituted aliphatic amines, quinoline-linked nitrogen/carbonyl rings, and fluorinated imino/carbonyl systems. There is substantial ring and aromatic chemistry, with narrower leader families within seeds. Digest ring-closure-string incidence ranges from 0.9598 to 0.9897 and aromatic-string incidence from 0.9517 to 0.9782. Those are molecule-level text incidences, not perceived ring counts or aromatic-atom fractions. Formal-charge and stereocentre-string incidences are 0.0 throughout, although aliphatic amines and potentially stereogenic centres are plainly present. All 15 Child and 15 published Parent trajectory paths were present and read, covering all five objectives and issued Search seeds 0, 1 and 2. Each node has 900 records per objective, including 870 accepted optimizer observations. No path, task or paired seed comparison is missing. context.comparison reports child_complete=true and paired_complete=true with no profile mismatch; the baseline is the published current-profile n-62daf219c70a. The full records, not only the digest late seed-2 proposals, establish the seed endpoints. The entire 300-record sessions for zaleplon_mpo seed 1, deco_hop seed 0 and median_2 seed 1 reproduce Parent evaluation/source/SMILES/score/best_so_far records exactly. Other sessions diverge chemically; exact endpoint ties alone were not used to claim identity. Read-only RDKit 2023.09.6 classification using the brief's declared neutral sulfur cases finds no absolute outside-envelope sulfur centres in the initial molecules or any of the 4350 Child optimizer observations. Parent has seven such optimizer observations, all in seed 2: three terminal nitrogen-sulfur-double cases in deco_hop, two unusual sulfur-valence cases in drd2_docking, and two in median_2. This is an absolute output description, not a reconstruction of parent-relative excess, rejection decisions or mechanism activation. The declared relative rule permits inherited outside-envelope signatures within their reference multiplicities; zero observed here is conditional on these trajectories and cannot be generalized to other starting populations. Sulfur is not removed: 1100 Child optimizer observations contain sulfur versus 935 Parent observations. Child sulfur centre counts are 734 divalent/hydrogen-bearing, 11 aromatic, 299 terminal carbon-double, 71 one-oxo and 86 two-oxo. These correspond respectively to 688, 11, 291, 71 and 77 molecule observations; a molecule can contain several centres or classes. The envelope permits sulfur-halogen bonds, N-S connections and thiocarbonyl groups, and constrains no non-sulfur atom. It establishes neither universal plausibility nor stability, safety, synthesis, pharmacology or geometry. Reactive local bonding, small-ring/bridged unsaturation and unspecified stereochemistry therefore keep overall synthetic plausibility questionable and drug-likeness weak, despite recognizable high-scoring azaaryl amides and cyclic aryl amines. Molecular sizes, motif counts and path hashes are documented in .slots/r0016-03-improve-L01/molecular/trajectory_chemistry_audit.json. All quoted complete SMILES are in the Child digest or trusted Child trajectories. Parent descriptions use its published trajectories and original molecular assessment. The score gradients are descriptive associations, not sulfur-specific effects, component attribution, or scores for rejected alternatives. Recurring gaps retain provenance in n-c55c3d520a2c through n-62daf219c70a; the n-93cd9a000278 envelope is a declared source condition, not pooled efficacy evidence.

per_task.generated_character: Leaders have 24-25 heavy atoms and three perceived rings. Seed 0 favors a divinyl/methyl-substituted azaindole-like fused system with an N-hydroxy aryl amide, no sulfur and no halogens. Seed 1 reproduces the Parent indole/pyridyl N-hydroxy amide with ring N-F and aryl chlorine. Seed 2 gives an N-H indole joined through adjacent thiocarbonyl/carbonyl groups to a pyridyl ring, plus methylamino and hydroxymethyl substituents. Sulfur remains present in 251 of 870 optimizer observations, versus Parent 150, predominantly divalent/H-bearing or terminal carbon-double forms. The leading sulfur-free azaaryl amide is comparatively recognizable chemistry, whereas N-halogen, N-S and adjacent thiocarbonyl/carbonyl variants require distinct local assessments. Median heavy-atom count is Child 24 versus Parent 25.
liabilities: N-F/N-Cl/N-Br ring substitution and halomethyl ethers remain outside the sulfur constraint. The N-hydroxy amide is recognizable chemistry and must not be conflated with the separate N-halogen bond.
The permitted N-S-H substituent and adjacent thiocarbonyl/carbonyl arrangement show that allowed sulfur does not imply routine stability or synthesis.
missing_features: Conventional local substitution is not consistently represented at the highest labels: 41 of the 50 highest Child optimizer observations still contain direct N-halogen bonds. The strong sulfur-free and halogen-free seed-0 leader is a counterexample to universal dependence.
Chemically independent plausible realizations of the compact aromatic/carbonyl arrangement remain limited among leaders; the observed record supplies no exact missing target pharmacophore.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-1744a1494180 versus its current-profile Parent n-62daf219c70a, on Search seeds 0, 1 and 2 at 300 observations per objective. No Child optimizer observation has an absolute outside-envelope sulfur centre, yet 93 of 4350 contain sulfur-halogen bonds, including high-scoring S-F or S-Br structures. A conventional methylthio analogue has a slightly higher label than its S-F relative. Other high-scoring families retain N-halogen, O-F, nitroso and N-S chemistry. The envelope is the exact declared n-93cd9a000278 neutral local condition; its source score effect is not transferred or pooled here. The broader local-bond gap was already recorded for n-c55c3d520a2c and n-62daf219c70a.
transferable_gaps.gap: A narrow sulfur envelope leaves substantial environment-dependent sulfur and non-sulfur reactivity unresolved in emitted molecules.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Distinguish intact functional-group environments and generate conventional alternatives preserving useful molecular arrangements. Treat a permitted local sulfur class as a narrow representation condition, not a safety, stability or synthesis certificate. Preserve useful thioethers, thiocarbonyls and oxides where feedback supports them. The observed chemistry neither proves that a broader filter improves scores nor attributes a residual motif to a specific component; inherited outside-envelope signatures remain allowed by the declared relative rule under other starting states.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Originally documented for n-c55c3d520a2c and reproduced in n-62daf219c70a, this persists in n-1744a1494180 on the complete current-profile Search panel at 300 observations per objective. Child output includes ring alkynes, an aromatic-labelled large nitrogen ring, unsaturated small nitrogen rings and dense small-ring closures. Cyclic cumulene incidence is lower in one fluorinated family, but its leaders exhibit different geometry concerns. Counterexamples include a compact azaaryl amide and a recognizable seven-membered cyclic aryl amine; ring richness itself is not missing.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently distinguish valence-valid ring graphs from geometrically credible unsaturation and connected-ring topology.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Ring transformations need sensitivity to ring size, bond geometry and bridge connectivity while offering feasible alternatives that retain learned functional relationships. Sulfur containment and aromatic labels supply none of that geometry information. Do not turn this into a blanket prohibition of small, fused, medium or macrocyclic rings. These output associations establish no causal score benefit or component-specific source of the problem.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The gap originating in n-c55c3d520a2c and carried by n-62daf219c70a is re-observed in n-1744a1494180 under the supplied current profile and Search seeds at 300 observations per objective. All digest stereocentre-string incidences are zero. RDKit perceives unassigned centres in 2455 of 4350 Child optimizer observations versus 2408 Parent observations. Some leaders have no perceived tetrahedral centre, so the issue applies where a generated structure requires stereochemical identity, not to every molecule.
transferable_gaps.gap: Potentially stereogenic molecular arrangements remain incompletely specified after generation.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve or resolve stereochemistry where chemically meaningful and treat achiral or configurationally unstable cases appropriately. Assess protonation and tautomerism separately; the neutral notation coexists with useful aliphatic amines. Neither the sulfur rule nor the scores establish a stereochemical penalty or identify which component caused the unspecified identity.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Originally reported for n-c55c3d520a2c and reproduced by n-62daf219c70a, this persists in the complete current-profile n-1744a1494180 panel at 300 observations per objective. Child emits 82 observations with at most three heavy atoms versus Parent 99. Tiny fragments commonly sit at floors, while larger aromatic concatenations with 39, 45, 68 or 96 heavy atoms fail to match corresponding compact leaders. The reduction in tiny fragments and successful compact azaaryl/cyclic-amine examples are counterexamples to uniform deterioration.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator inconsistently preserves useful functional-group context while avoiding fragmentation and excessive elaboration.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Use accepted task-local feedback to retain useful combinations of chemical regions when shrinking, expanding or reconnecting molecules. Allow genuine simplification and useful growth; neither a fixed minimum size nor preference for more aromatic mass follows from the evidence. This remains a conditional molecular-context gap, not an attribution to crossover or proof that size restrictions improve endpoints.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The n-c55c3d520a2c gap carried through n-62daf219c70a remains conditional evidence in n-1744a1494180 under the current profile and complete Search panel at 300 observations per objective. Leading series repeatedly vary halogen placement, short chains, sulfur/carbonyl groups or connected-ring segments. Different seeds do reach distinct families, including a comparatively conventional halogen-free azaaryl amide, and three complete sessions reproduce Parent molecules exactly. The evidence therefore supports limited local alternatives rather than global scaffold collapse.
transferable_gaps.gap: Plausible independent alternatives to a successful local scaffold family are not consistently represented among leading molecules.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Offer chemically independent, feasible connectivities retaining favorable relationships learned from current observations, and assess their labels and chemistry separately. Distinct strings or envelope membership alone do not establish useful coverage. This condition does not justify objective-specific target scaffolds, a component attribution, or a guaranteed benefit from increasing diversity.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
